# Bone

- Inherits [`Attachment`](attachment.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Bone")`

An attachment that follows one joint of the skinned `MeshPart` it is parented to. Use it to weld a sword to a hand, hang a light from a moving arm, or read where a foot is: it moves with the animation.

Bones are not created automatically. Create one for each joint you need and set its `JointName`. A bone whose `JointName` does not match a joint in the rig follows the `MeshPart` itself.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `JointIndex` | `number` | `-1` | read-only | The index of the joint that `JointName` matched, or -1 if the rig has no joint of that name. It is looked up again when the mesh reloads. |
| `JointName` | `string` | — | read/write | The name of the joint this bone follows, as it is named in the model file of the parent `MeshPart`. |
| `Transform` | `CFrame` | — | read/write | An offset added to the joint's animated pose, in the joint's own space. Use it for procedural animation on top of a clip: bend an arm toward a target, turn a head, kick a weapon back on a shot. The identity, the default, leaves the pose unchanged. |
